Nicholas (27)
McGarvey (42)
Dundee Utd (0) 1
Milne (82)
Att:- 27,000
Celtic won deservedly on a cold frosty day despite a Dundee United late fight back to keep the pressure on league leaders Aberdeen.
Celtic adapted to the hard underfoot conditions with Provan and Sullivan being influential on Celtic's right flank.
The opening goal came when Tommy Burns made a fine diagonal run into the area on to a Dom Sullivan pass. He ran to the right hand bye line and whipped over a cross with his weaker right foot and McGarvey spectacularly adjusted his body to head powerfully past Hamish McAlpine.
McGarvey and Nicholas were now a magnificent partnership and a constant threat in front of goal and it was Nicholas who scored the second with an opportunist effort. McAlpine sent a poor goal kick out to Celtic's left and Burns cleverly headed the ball over the United defence catching them square. Nicholas was just onside and ran forward to delicately lob McAlpine for a superb goal.
After half time Celtic tired and United began to creep back in to the game. Substitute Ralph Milne caused trouble with his pace and he pulled a goal back in 82 minutes. Celtic panicked after this and it took some fine defending by McGrain and good handling by Bonner to see them through to the final whistle.

sections.review:
Celtic produced one of their best performances of the season in difficult conditions when snow fell during the match.
Rangers took the lead in 11 minutes through Derek Johnstone when he headed in a swerving Cooper cross. It remained that way until half time despite bad misses from Tommy Burns and Tom McAdam. Celtic took more control of the game in the second half and Provan, Nicholas and McGarvey were a real handful for the Rangers defence.
Charlie Nicholas got a fine double in 57 and 73 minutes to put Celtic 2-1 up and Celtic continued to dominate with McGarvey missing two sitters. Then with 3 minutes to go, Roy Aitken, after a fine strong run from defence, tried to pass to McGarvey, but the ball rebounded of Colin Jackson and into his path and he smashed the ball high, past McCloy to give Celtic a 3-1 victory.
Celtic's second half performance had been truly outstanding with young Mark Reid deserving of a mention on his Old Firm debut. Had McGarvey not missed two sitters in the second half then the margin of victory would have been greater.

One Kenny Ashwood, there’s only one Kenny Ashwood, one Kenny Ashwood, there’s only one Kenny Ashwood!
During a dull moment the Celtic crowd turned their attention to a particularly small player in East Stirling colours. Out of amusement the Jungle began to cheer the East Stirling players’ every touch particularly this one wee guy in the number 10 shirt. The programme listed the player as Kenny Ashwood when in fact the wee guy concerned was Bobby McCulley. Ashwood was running around Parkhead totally perplexed to why the Jungle should be chanting his name, meanwhile McCulley became something of a minor celebrity in Scottish football circles afterwards, being named as Scotland’s smallest player at 5 feet 2 inches after his Parkhead appearance.

sections.review:
Celtic (3) 7   
Aitken 12
McGarvey 37 45 57
Nicholas 47
McCluskey 88 90
St.Mirren (0) 0
Att: 18,000
Celtic, in a rich vein of form and playing in their change strip of green with white diamonds, absolutely demolished a decent St Mirren side at Parkhead.
Star of the show was ex Saints star Frank McGarvey who fired a sensational hat trick past Scotland goalkeeper Billy Thomson.
Roy Aitken had headed Celts into an early lead before McGarvey took hold of proceedings. He robbed Alex Beckett in the Saints penalty area and fired past Thomson but better was to come. On the stroke of half time he gathered a ball 30 yards out and beat Beckett before centre half Fulton attempted to tackle him, he lost his balance but deftly kept control and then unleashed a glorious powerful drive into the top corner from 25 yards.
The Celtic crowd went into raptures and were still cheeering as the referee blew for half time with McGarvey given his own personal ovation and it is said that McGarvey was actually physically sick with the excitement in the dressing room.
In the second half Nicholas scored early on and received a bad injury from Fulton in the process and had to be carried off, with George McCluskey replacing him. McGarvey completed his hat trick after that after another defensive error and McCluskey added two late goals amidst a downpour of rain, from great work by McGrain firstly and then Tommy Burns.
Celtic's day was rounded off when MacLeod came on as a substitute, his first appearance after a long absence through injury.
The fans cheered loudly at time up as Hearts victory over Rangers at Tynecastle was announced on the loudspeaker.
Saints persevered to the end and had fine efforts at goal from Weir, Stark and Bone but goalkeeper Bonner and a bit of bad luck prevented a consolation goal.

sections.review:
Celtic (0) 1   
McCluskey (85)
Aberdeen (1) 1
Harrow (17)
Att:- 35,200.
A large crowd turned out on a blustery March day to see if Aberdeen could keep their title hopes alive or if Celtic could storm further ahead in the race for the championship.
Celtic started brightly but Aberdeen took the lead against the run of play when Harrow, their recent signing from Luton, scored on a swift break with the Celtic defence posted missing.
Aberdeen continued to frustrate Celtic although Provan hit a post before half time. Aberdeen looked as if they were missing the influence and subtle touches of the injured pair of Gordon Strachan and John McMaster in midfield.
In the second half Celtic turned up the pressure with the game taking on a cup tie feeling, and George McCluskey was particularly impressive when he replaced Nicholas. The heavy conditions were sapping the players' strength and Celtic were awarded a penalty in 68 minutes after a foul by Watson on Murdo MacLeod. MacLeod himself took the penalty but tried placing it and Leighton was able to save easily.
Mark McGhee was still a danger on the break and Bonner saved well before McGhee claimed for a penalty after a challenge from McAdam.
Celtic gave their all in the closing stages and the equaliser came in 88 minutes after a sparkling run and cross from Provan that was volleyed home by McCluskey. With the Celtic fans in a fervour their team attacked again and McCluskey thought he had claimed the winner after great work from Frank McGarvey but he was controversially given offside although TV pictures were to show that he was marginally on.

sections.trivia:
Celtic win the league

Celtic take a title bow on an unseasonably cold night in Dundee. 
  Celtic officially became League Champions for the thirty-second time. 
  It was a magnificent performance at Tannadice, which was taken over by thousands of Celtic fans. 
  MacLeod’s goal in 2 minutes was Celtic’s 80th League goal of the season. A new record. 
  Celtic players carry Danny McGrain shoulder high around Tannadice.
The eighth meeting of the season between Celtic and Dundee United. 
Richard Gough made his senior debut in football on this night as a substitute.
"With Supporters like these, how can you fail to become champions? They are just incredible. I give Celtic credit for playing really well and beating us but these fans look as though they are part of the team."
Jim McLean, Dundee Utd Manager and Scottish football legend
sections.review:
This game was the highlight of the season and Burns' goal is candidate for goal of the season. Celtic win the title in entertaining fashion by playing attacking football.
The celebrations at full time are emotional as McGrain and McNeill are carried shoulder high by the players.

sections.memories:
I was at this game. Before the kick-off I was slightly surprised that the Jags fans around me were supremely confident of success. They weren't basing this prediction on recent results because Celtic had not only beaten Thistle in all four league games but had also knocked the Maryhill Magyars out of the League Cup. No, through a unique brand of Firhill logic. their optimism was based entirely on the fact that Thistle tended to win trophies only in years ending in a one!
Their solitary Scottish Cup win happened in 1921, their last Glasgow Cup win had been in 1961 and of course they were still celebrating their sensational League Cup success of 1971. Alan Rough and Jackie Campbell had played in that Hampden final and both of them played a crucial part in the Thistle line-up ten years later.
It wasn't a bad game and there was enough of a crowd to give the game a respectable sense of occasion. Celtic started strongly and always looked far more likely to score. Splendid goalkeeping and resolute defending from the home team seemed only to be delaying the inevitable. But once Ian Jardine had given Partick the lead, there was a growing feeling that, in spite of incessant Celtic pressure., it was going to be Thistle's night. The Jags contested every challenge as if they were playing in a European Cup final while Celtic, although making some sort of an effort, nevertheless looked like a team that was just taking care of a few last chores after having clinched the League Championship a week and a half before. The immoveable object stood firm as the irresistible force eventually wheezed to a standstill. 
And so it was that when the final whistle blew, the Scottish champions had to stand back and watch the undeniably grand old trophy being handed over to, as it were, Glasgow's finest in accordance with the unbreakable laws of esoteric numerology and astrological divination.
(by user HenryClarson of TheCelticWiki)
